title: Jesus and Mary in Islam
hook: "So you don't believe in Jesus anymore?" You do. Here's what Muslims believe, and how to say it kindly.

screens.text: If your family is Christian, this question is coming, maybe from a grandparent who loves you: "So you don't believe in Jesus anymore?" The honest answer is that you do. Today: how Muslims see him, and how to say it kindly.
**Muslims love Jesus and Mary.** In Arabic they're ***'Isa*** and ***Maryam***. A whole chapter of the Qur'an is named after Mary [Q 19:16].
bubbles: The Qur'an says Allah chose Mary above the women of all the worlds [Q 3:42].
Muslims say "peace be upon him" after Jesus's name, just as they do for every prophet.

screens.prompt: What do Muslims believe about Jesus?

items.text: He was born of a virgin
items.why: Yes. An angel brought Mary the news, and she asked how, when no man had touched her [Q 3:45–47].
Yes. The Qur'an calls him the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary [Q 3:45].

items.text: He healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead

items.why: Yes. Muslims believe Allah gave him the Gospel (Injil), with guidance and light [Q 5:46].

items.text: He is the son of God
items.why: The real difference: he is a messenger and servant of Allah, who has no son [Q 4:171; Q 19:30; Q 112:3].

items.text: He was killed on the cross
items.why: The Qur'an says he wasn't killed or crucified, but that Allah raised him up to Himself [Q 4:157–158].

screens.text: **Lots of common ground, one real difference.** Muslims and Christians share a lot: Mary's purity, the virgin birth, the miracles, the Messiah. The difference is who Jesus is: for Muslims, a beloved prophet and servant of Allah, not God or God's son.
bubbles: You can say that honestly without attacking anyone's faith.

screens.prompt: Grandma asks, "So you don't believe in Jesus anymore?" What's a good first answer?

options.text: "I do, Grandma. Muslims love Jesus. We believe he's a great prophet, born to Mary by a miracle."
options.feedback: Right. Start with what you share. It's true, and it's what she most needs to hear.
Not quite. That starts a fight and hurts someone who loves you. Lead with common ground.

options.text: "I don't want to talk about it."
options.feedback: Sometimes okay, but here a short, warm answer can ease her worry a lot.

steps.text: **Listen first.** Often the real question is "Are you still ours?" Answer that too.
**Start with common ground.** Jesus, Mary, one God, prayer, family.
**Be honest about the difference**, briefly and gently. No debate at the dinner table.
**Respect their faith.** It raised you. Gentle words open doors [Q 16:125].

screens.prompt: Build a warm first answer to "Do you still believe in Jesus?"
screens.answer: Yes, Muslims love Jesus as a great prophet
screens.feedback: That's it: true, short and kind. Common ground first.

screens.character: Grandma Ruth, your Christian grandmother, who loves you and is worried
screens.setup: You're helping her in the kitchen. She sets down a dish and says softly: "Honey, your mom told me you became Muslim. Do you still believe in Jesus? I pray for you every night."
screens.goal: Reassure her that you love her, explain what Muslims believe about Jesus and Mary in simple words, and keep the relationship warm.
screens.success_looks_like: You thank her for praying for you, share the common ground (Jesus as a beloved prophet, Mary's honor, the virgin birth), state the difference briefly and kindly, and don't criticize her faith.
screens.coach_notes: Ruth is gentle, devout and a little hurt. She may ask: "But Jesus is the son of God," "Will you still come to church at Christmas?" or "Did someone pressure you?" She never mocks or threatens. Debrief: praise warmth and common ground; flag any moment that sounded like debating or putting down her faith; offer one kind sentence for the hardest question. For Christmas questions, point to the holiday module and the imam.

chips: How do I explain the Trinity difference without arguing?
What does the Qur'an say about Mary?
My grandma says she prays for me. How do I respond?
Can I still go to church events with family?

screens.text: Read Mary's story in the Qur'an.
steps: Open an English translation to Surah Maryam (chapter 19)
screens.optional_extra: If you have Christian family, think of one thing you share with them about Jesus that you could say next time it comes up.

screens.text: Muslims love and honor Jesus and Mary. Lead with that; share the difference about who he is gently and briefly.
Your family's faith shaped you. Being kind about it is part of your own.

prayerPhrase.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
prayerPhrase.translit: Allahumma barik 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka hamidun majid
prayerPhrase.meaning: O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family, as You blessed Ibrahim (Abraham) and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
prayerPhrase.when: Salat Ibrahimiyya part 2, right after part 1, in the last sitting only [Bukhari 3370]. Notice Ibrahim: Abraham, honored by Jews, Christians and Muslims alike, is remembered in every prayer.

check.prompt: Which of these do Muslims believe about Jesus?

options.text: He was born of the virgin Mary and is a great prophet and the Messiah
options.feedback: Right. The Qur'an teaches the virgin birth and calls him the Messiah [Q 3:45–47].
Not quite. Believing in Jesus as a prophet is part of Islam.

options.text: He is the son of God
options.feedback: Not quite. Muslims believe he is a messenger and servant of Allah, who has no son [Q 4:171].

check.prompt: A Christian relative asks about your faith. What's the best way to start?

options.text: With what you share: Jesus, Mary, one God, prayer
options.feedback: Right. Common ground first; the difference, gently and briefly, after.

options.text: With the problems in their beliefs
options.feedback: Not quite. That usually ends the conversation and hurts the relationship.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Mary: chosen and purified above the women of the worlds [Q 3:42]; Surah 19 is named after her and tells her story [Q 19:16–36].
- Jesus: born of the virgin Mary [Q 3:45–47]; called the Messiah [Q 3:45]; miracles by Allah's permission [Q 3:49]; given the Gospel (Injil) [Q 5:46]; a messenger and servant of Allah [Q 4:171; Q 19:30]; Allah has no son [Q 4:171; Q 112].
- The Qur'an says Jesus was not killed or crucified, and Allah raised him to Himself [Q 4:157–158]. State it plainly and briefly; don't speculate on details.
- Talking with Christian family: listen, common ground first, the difference briefly and kindly, never mock [Q 16:125; Spec §6.2 rule 8].
- Prayer phrase: Salat Ibrahimiyya part 2 [Bukhari 3370].

**Likely questions**
- *"How do I explain the Trinity difference?"* One sentence: "Muslims believe God is one, with no partners or son, and that Jesus is His messenger." No arguments about the Bible's text.
- *"Grandma says she prays for me."* Suggest thanking her sincerely ("That means a lot") and saying they pray for her too. Kindness, not correction.
- *"Can I go to church events?"* Family events and meals: yes, keep ties. Taking part in worship rites is the question: give the general picture and route specifics (Christmas, funerals, weddings) to the imam [Q5 territory; the holiday-christmas module covers it].
- *"Do Muslims believe Jesus will come back?"* Yes: Muslims believe he will return before the Last Day and rule with justice [Bukhari 3448]. Keep it brief, and don't repeat that hadith's details about the cross to Christian family; they're easily misheard as an insult.
- *"Is the Bible true?"* Muslims believe Allah revealed the Torah and Gospel [Q 3:3; Q 5:46], and Day 37 covers the books. Don't disparage the Bible.

**Escalate:** attending specific church services or rites; a family member who threatens or cuts off the convert (safety first if needed).

**Don't**
- Don't mock or belittle Christian beliefs, the Bible, or the cross.
- Don't give a ruling on Christmas or church attendance (Q5).
- Don't make claims about anyone's salvation or afterlife.

**Role-play brief:** Grandma Ruth is devout, loving, a little hurt. Asks about Jesus as the son of God, Christmas, pressure. Never hostile. Debrief on warmth, common ground and avoiding debate.
